description: POST /sessions/{id}/action: one step. x and y with coords "screenshot" are pixels on the latest screenshot, which the host scales back to the page. A point wins over an element when a step has both. A step settles before the host answers. Neither host ends a settle for quiet, or for a step that started nothing, before settle_quiet_ms from its start, so a request the step starts by then (a search box's debounced suggestions) is waited for. A step that by then has changed nothing, started no main-frame request or navigation and left nothing shown marked aria-busy answers there. One that started a main-frame request or a navigation, or finds the page aria-busy, waits until those requests are done, nothing shown is marked aria-busy and the page has shown no change for settle_quiet_ms, at most settle_max_ms from the settle's start. One that only changed the page in place waits for that quiet at most settle_quiet_ms past the host's first look at the page after the step, so a page that changes on its own (a ticker) doesn't hold every step to the cap. A navigation's cap is each host's own. The router's browser waits up to 5 s each for a navigation to commit and for its new page's DOMContentLoaded (a navigate step's own load has waited up to 30 s for it), then for the new page's network to go idle too, and stops at the later of settle_max_ms from the settle's start and 1.5 s after that DOMContentLoaded wait, never past 31.5 s from the step's start. The desktop app's browser waits for a navigate, back, forward or reload step's page to finish loading, up to 30 s, before the settle, and stops every settle, a navigation's too, at settle_max_ms from its start. changed says whether the step changed what the page shows: true, false, or null when the host can't tell (a frame, canvas or media element in view or under the step, a closed shadow root, a hover, a wait, a read, or a page it couldn't watch). The answer carries the page after the step when include_page is true. into_frame is true only when the person approved this one step on a card and its point may land in a frame, whatever held it. The desktop app's browser, which holds no steps itself, refuses (409) a press, or a drag's release, that lands in a frame when into_frame is false or missing; the router's browser holds its own steps and ignores it.
